narrative.overview: Tenho Dado looks like the table after the dice have landed: near-black, lit by a single warm amber, with the loser's name written in red. It is a working surface, not a stage. The page frame is quiet; the score rows are dense and exact. Numbers, names, dates, and amounts are set in DM Sans with tabular figures, because the group reads this board to settle a debt and settle an argument. Bebas Neue appears only when the table announces something — the page title or the loser.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black tonal surfaces (ink-950 → ink-900 → ink-800), no shadows.
Hairline 1px borders instead of elevation; rows instead of nested cards.
One warm accent for money and state; one red for loss.
Bebas Neue for announcements, DM Sans for every readable value.
Tabular numerals everywhere a column must stay still.
Phone-first at the table, wider report columns on desktop.
44px touch controls and reflow down to 320px.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber marks money and state. It occupies a small share of any screen; its rarity is what makes it read as the table light, not a brand wash.

rules.name: The Red Name Rule
rules.body: Red belongs to the loser, the loss, and the destructive action. It is never used for decoration, headings, or an inactive control.

rules.name: The Display Is Not Data Rule
rules.body: Bebas Neue is for announcements. Every number, name, date, amount, and table cell is DM Sans. If a value must be compared down a column, it is tabular and it is not display type.

rules.name: The Label Is a Whisper Rule
rules.body: Labels are small, uppercase, tracked, and ink-400. They name the value; they never repeat it or shout over it.

rules.name: The Two-Line Player Rule
rules.body: A player row has a name line and a meta line. The name is primary; the meta is secondary. Never merge them into one line.

rules.name: The One Border Rule
rules.body: Declare elevation once. A surface gets a border or a shadow, never both; this system chooses the border.

rules.name: The No-Nested-Cards Rule
rules.body: If a card needs cards inside it, the hierarchy is wrong. Use rows separated by borders.

dos: Do use ink-* tokens for every surface, border, and text tone; the app is dark-only by product decision.
Do use DM Sans with tabular-nums for every value that can be compared down a column.
Do lead a game card with the loser and the amount.
Do keep all touch controls at 44px, including tabs, presets, back, and inline actions.
Do declare grid-cols-1 before a md:grid-cols-* or lg:grid-cols-* breakpoint.
Do let long names truncate in rows and wrap in the game headline.
Do keep amber for money/state and red for loss/destructive action.
Do use one border, one radius family, and no shadow.
donts: Don't set Bebas Neue on numbers, names, dates, amounts, or table cells.
Don't use fixed pixel sizes for durable type roles; use rem so user font settings apply.
Don't nest cards or add a second surface to a card to create hierarchy.
Don't add box shadows, glow, gradient text, or colored left rails.
Don't use amber for non-money/non-state decoration or red for chrome.
Don't animate width, height, or margins for bars; use transforms.
Don't use emoji or Unicode dice as functional icons.
Don't rely on color alone: pair a loss with the loser's name and a spend with a currency value.
Don't switch the app to a light theme or introduce a second accent without a product decision.
